reviewCriteria: Follow the concrete consumer request, source and resource owner before choosing Iterator, Stream or Spliterator.

Preserve correct pull/removal semantics with lookahead, optional removal, exhaustion and failures.
Distinguish requested prefix, proven source exhaustion and incomplete traversal under fixed event/time budgets.
Preserve already-visible consumer effects and explicit cleanup on early exit/failure without inventing rollback or cancellation.
Keep characteristics and splitting claims true, preserve Java17 examples and qualify optional Java24 Gatherers.

findingsAdequatelyCovered.finding: Resource ownership, optional removal, lookahead interference, fail-fast limitations and weak/snapshot semantics are already explicit.
findingsAdequatelyCovered.consequence: The tested best-effort fail-fast and delegated-removal counterexamples are anticipated by existing guidance.

findingsAdequatelyCovered.finding: Unknown-size bounded traversal uses ORDERED|NONNULL, trySplit null, explicit deadline/interruption/fetch failure, and throws when an event cap cannot establish exhaustion.
findingsAdequatelyCovered.consequence: The source cap does not falsely signal normal end-of-source. A requested prefix remains a legitimate distinct contract.

findingsAdequatelyCovered.finding: Remote cursor consistency, close scope, close-versus-cancellation and iterator-owner obligations are qualified.
findingsAdequatelyCovered.consequence: No snapshot, rollback or transport cancellation guarantee is inferred from a wrapper or terminal operation.
